sheets.prompt: Interior concept art for a science fiction exploration game: the Builders' Greenhouse in a meadow hollow of the garden world Viridel, the house where a vanished people told the garden to go on growing. Its makers were never human: gardeners who fed on light as plants do, and they built a house for steering sunlight, not for walking in. There are no columns, frames, panes, stairs or doorways of human shape. The house is a cluster of huge translucent cells like a heap of soap foam or frogspawn, each bubble-wall thin, pearly and faintly green, meeting its neighbours in soft curved seams; the sun comes through all of them. Hanging inside the cells, great round liquid lenses like drops of water slowly turn and swing beams of sunlight across the hall, one beam falling on a carved white eye. A deep chasm splits the floor of the largest cell; at its near edge a living vine bridge has just grown from a seed, leaves and pink blossoms unfurling across the gap; on the far side a second vine climbs a smooth cell wall to a great closed flower bud filling a round opening. In a shaded cell kneels the Gardener, a moss giant on root legs with a smooth white stone mask for a face, dormant. The makers' sign, three dots over an arc that bows upward, set where three cells meet. A cloaked adult human traveller of ordinary height with a round jade fluid backpack stands at the chasm's edge, a stream of leaf green and petal pink glowing fluid arcing onto the seed, dwarfed by the foam. Moebius science-fiction, Franco-Belgian ligne claire, exquisite fine pen contours, sparse delicate hatching only in shadows, luminous flat pastel gouache colours, white, leaf green, petal pink, pearly sunlit cells, sky blue, soft blue shadows, restrained cream paper grain, clear readable construction, no lettering. Avoid: photorealism, 3d render, text, watermark, lettering, labels, glass panes, metal frame, columns.
